messages:
maria: Heads-up — nightly eval flagged a big drop for the INT8 precision profile on the summarization suite (run 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC). Rouge-L down ~6.2 vs FP16 baseline. Sample of failing prompt attached.
kevin: ugh. which model + quant-config? did it start after the new kernel change? :thinking_face:
maria: Model: rwdw-3b-v1 (baseline FP16). INT8 profile built with post-training static quant (calib_samples=128, per_channel=true, per_tensor_clamp=false). Nightly switched to that profile automatically via rollout policy last night.
tom: do we have a diff of calib distribution vs previous night? small sample sizes can bias dynamic range estimates.
maria: attaching excerpt from eval logs:

```
[eval-summary]
metric: ROUGE_L
fp16: 0.412
int8: 0.350
delta: -0.062
calib_samples: 128
skew: topk prompt set 27% outliers
```

Example failing generation (shortened):

User prompt: "Summarize the following meeting notes about infra cost optimization..."
FP16 output: "We should batch small requests, enable KV caching, and adjust autoscaler thresholds."
INT8 output: "The meeting was about costs. Action: review."

kevin: that looks like compression of informative tokens -> quantization saturation. Did the calibration see representative long-form contexts? 128 might be too low for this distribution.

anjali: running a targeted repro now with calib_samples=1024 and with per_tensor_clamp=true to compare. will push results in ~20m.

eval-bot: nightly-eval v2 completed. new alert created: #2170009432-nightly-int8-anomaly (severity: medium). Linked metrics pinned to thread.

tom: also check the token-level activation ranges for attention heads 7 and 12 — those were noisy in the earlier sweep.

maria: good call. grabbing activation histograms from the last run. snippet:

```
layer_7_attn_q max: 6.1 -> int8 clip at 5.5
layer_12_attn_k max: 4.8 -> int8 clip at 4.0
```

maria: hypothesis: calibration sample had disproportionately short prompts, so extreme activations truncated and value mapping clipped high-information tokens.

kevin: two quick checks if anjali repro is slower:
1) rerun calibration with stratified sampling over prompt length (short/med/long buckets)
2) try post-training quant with bias correction (symmetric->asymmetric switch)

anjali: ran both. preliminary numbers:
- calib_samples=1024, stratified: ROUGE_L = 0.403 (delta -0.009 vs FP16)
- bias-corrected asymmetric: ROUGE_L = 0.408 (delta -0.004 vs FP16)

anjali: so stratified + asymmetric bias correction looks promising. saving the quant profile as qc/2170009432/strat-asym.json

tom: awesome. can we add a quick A/B in prod-sim with 1% traffic to validate behavioral differences on live queries? and add a regression test to nightly to include length-stratified calibration for models that show >0.03 delta.

maria: +1. I'll open a rollout ticket and add the new profile to the canary list. If prod-sim looks good we'll promote.

kevin: log a root cause note: "calibration sample skew -> clipping of long-context activations -> compressed informative tokens". Also add remediation: increase calib sample size and stratified sampling, enable asymmetric calibration as default for this architecture until further notice.

maria: created ticket INF-4923 with the findings and linked this thread. tagging @kevin @tom for review.

eval-bot: test-run scheduled: repro-int8-stratified-1024 at 2026-03-20T02:45:00Z. Results will post here.

anjali: quick note — we should also check FP8 baseline runs. FP8 may preserve dynamic range better for those heads and be cheaper than reverting to FP16.

kevin: agreed. add FP8 smoke in the comparison matrix and capture latency/cost tradeoffs.

maria: thanks all, will follow up with the canary plan. :thumbsup:
